::: {#exr-information-gain}
#### Choosing between two splits

A node holds $20$ points, $10$ red and $10$ green.
Two candidate splits each send the points into two branches:

| split | branch | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | yes | $4$ | $0$ |
| | no | $6$ | $10$ |
| B | yes | $5$ | $10$ |
| | no | $5$ | $0$ |

Draw one point from the node, each equally likely,
let $Y$ be its color, and let $X$ be the branch it falls into
(@rem-information-gain).
The [information gain](#def-information-gain) of each split is then $\mutinfof{X}{Y}$.
Use base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) throughout.

1. Compute $H(Y)$.

2. For each split, compute $H(Y \mid X = x)$ for both branches,
   and then $H(Y \mid X)$.

3. Compute the information gain $\mutinfof{X}{Y}$ for each split.
   Which split has the larger gain?

:::
